LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's global/top-level scope consists only of static metadata assignments: `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `makedepends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `options`, `source`, and `sha256sums`. There are no command substitutions, no `eval`, no encoded/obfuscated strings, and no network or file operations executed at source time. Sourcing this file to run `makepkg --printsrcinfo` therefore only defines variables and the packaging functions; nothing malicious executes.

The `source` entry fetches the package's own declared upstream (`git+https://github.com/hyperpuncher/pi-ui.git`, branch `main`) and is marked `sha256sums=('SKIP')`. That is ordinary VCS packaging practice and is not grounds to fail this gate (no download/verification occurs at `--printsrcinfo`; the unpinned branch/SKIP is noted for the later full audit). The potentially heavier operations (`bun ci`, `bun run build`, `bun run test`, `install`) live only inside `prepare()`/`build()`/`check()`/`package()` and do not run during metadata parsing. Nothing here deviates from standard packaging and no injected/obfuscated/exfiltrating code is present at sourcing time.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Global scope only defines variables; no execution during printsrcinfo.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
